sentences.text: This ancient bird measured roughly twenty centimetres in length, with an axial column preserved at eighty-seven millimetres.
It weighed between fifteen and twenty grammes and possessed a single claw on each wing.
Its ribcage lacked ossified uncinate processes, though cartilaginous versions likely existed.
A single claw on each wing was a unique trait for this small flyer.
Its feet featured three forward-pointing toes and one backward toe, marking it as an early arboreal bird.
Armando Díaz Romeral found the fossil in 1985 at Las Hoyas in east central Spain.
José Luis Sanz and José Fernando Bonaparte named the species Iberomesornis romerali in 1992.
As a constant flyer, its shorter tail and higher shoulder position aided in swooping and turning at speed.
It inhabited the edges of a large shallow lake teeming with fish, turtles, and crocodiles.
Evidence suggests its diet included small insects and crustaceans.
Today, it is classified within Ornithothoraces as a basal member of the Enantiornithes family Iberomesornithidae.
The species shows derived physical characteristics when compared to Archaeopteryx.
This bird lived during the Barremian, from 125.77 to 121.4 million years ago.
Because the skull is missing, scientists cannot be certain about its diet, even though no purely herbivorous bird has been found.
